course_name_original: Teoría de Circuitos y Máquinas Eléctricas
prerequisites: Resolution of linear equation systems and quadratic equations (used in the study of electrical circuits)
Knowledge of exponential and logarithmic functions
Knowledge and handling of complex number calculations (very important)
Ability to apply fundamental physics principles

learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge and use of the principles of circuit theory and electrical machines.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, abilities, and skills in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Ability to handle specifications, regulations, and mandatory standards.
Know and analyze the electrical circuits that make up electrical installations. Understand the main components that are part of linear electrical circuits.
Know and analyze the electrical networks that supply energy to an industrial installation. Understand the main methods for solving electrical networks.

Know and understand the operation of the various electrical machines, both rotary and static, that may appear in a typical installation. Understand the different sets of rotary and static electrical machines to know their operating principle, practical utility, and selection criteria for specific applications.
Apply resolution methods that allow knowing electrical magnitudes in any part of the circuit. Evaluate currents, voltages, or powers of any load connected to the network.
Apply methods to obtain optimal and/or regulatory dimensions that ensure the proper functioning of electrical networks. Evaluate different practical cases regarding their arrangement and operation.
Integrate electrical machine devices into an installation optimally. Evaluate the safety levels they implement and the needs implied by their use.

Develop professional skills and attitudes: adopt a critical stance on real-world problems, foster engineer's creativity, seek effective and lowest-cost solutions. Apply an attitude of responsibility, leadership, and commitment to work.

syllabus_topics: Single-phase alternating current. Basic laws. Circuit analysis.
Rotary electrical machines. Safety and Lighting.
teaching_methods: Solving exercises proposed in participatory lectures
Solving practical cases proposed in practical sessions
Preparation of reports for practical activities
Synchronous and/or asynchronous online sessions (contingency plan)
Innovative teaching activities within the teaching project "ConectaIA: Active learning and digital competencies through Artificial Intelligence"

assessment_methods.method: Practical activities (laboratory practice report or equivalent) (SE11)

assessment_rules: The final grade is calculated as 0.2 * Practical activities + 0.7 * Exam + 0.1 * In-class tests. A minimum score of 5 points must be obtained in both practical activities and the exam. If this minimum is not met, the average will not be calculated, and the course will be failed with the higher score of the unpassed part between the exam and practical activities. For the extraordinary call, students who completed continuous assessment during the course will retain their grades, while others will take an exam covering 100% of the grade. For the single final evaluation, the grade is 0.8 * Exam + 0.2 * Practical test, requiring a minimum of 5 in the exam.
